metadata.title: AI for Climate Adaptation

beats.narration_text: Ola. Climate change is not a future problem anymore. Floods, heat waves and droughts are already here. So the question today is simple: how can AI actually help people adapt? And where does it fall short?

props.command: How can AI help communities adapt to floods, heat and drought? And where does it fall short?
output: See danger earlier: floods, heat, drought.
Aim help where it is needed most.
Limits: data gaps, the last mile, energy.

beats.narration_text: AI will not stop climate change. But it can help us live with it, by helping people see floods, heat and drought coming early enough to act. That is the whole idea.

props.text:
AI will fix
climate change.
It warns us early.

qc.sparse_reason: hesitant-writer typing bookend: text accumulates token by token, so mid-beat frames are mostly cream by design

beats.narration_text: First, two different jobs. Mitigation cuts emissions, so the planet warms less. Adaptation prepares for the warming we can no longer avoid: bigger floods, hotter cities, drier fields. This video is about the second job. And adaptation is really a prediction problem. That is where AI earns its place.

show.event: adaptation column fills: floods, heat, drought icons

beats.narration_text: Start with floods. Rain, river levels and satellite data flow into a model that learns how a river behaves. The payoff is time. A warning that arrives days ahead, not hours, means families can move and farmers can save their animals. AI forecasts now reach places that have very few river gauges.

show.event: three data sources flow into a model box
timeline: flood day marked; old warning hours before
AI warning slides back to days before, terracotta

beats.narration_text: Now heat. In one city, two streets a short walk apart can differ by several degrees. Satellite images and AI can map the hottest blocks, street by street. Then the city knows exactly where to plant trees, add shade or open a cooling center, instead of spreading help thin.

show.event: blocks warm up into a heat map
hottest blocks outlined; trees and cooling-center markers drop in

qc.sparse_reason: build-up beat: heat map first, then the three actions slide in; the 50% frame catches the partial build

beats.narration_text: On farms, AI reads weather forecasts, soil moisture and satellite views of crops, and turns them into simple advice. Water this field now. This one can wait. Plant a week later. For a small farmer facing a drier season, that advice can decide whether there is a harvest at all.

show.event: advice tags appear under each field; driest field's tag in terracotta

beats.narration_text: Now the honest part. One: data gaps. The places hit hardest often have the fewest sensors. Two: the last mile. A perfect warning is useless if it never reaches the person who needs it. Three: energy. Big models use power too. So AI can warn. People still have to act.

show.event: card 2: last mile, a broken arrow to a house
line: 'AI warns. People act.' with terracotta 'act'

qc.sparse_reason: build-up beat: the three limit cards land one per narration point; mid-beat frames show the partial set

beats.narration_text: The verdict. AI helps adaptation by seeing risk earlier and in finer detail. It does not replace good data, trusted local networks, or the people who act on a warning.

props.artifactHeading: What AI can and cannot do

Farms: turn weather and soil data into advice.
Limits: data gaps, the last mile, energy.
